exercises.title: Usage-centric 1 — usage-centric or product-centric?
exercises.problemHtml:
Usage-centric: understand what users need to accomplish, then derive the functionality. Product-centric: define features you expect will sell — riskier, since you may build features nobody uses. Classify each way of working.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.

exercises.title: Usage-centric 2 — use case and user story
exercises.problemHtml:
A use case is a sequence of interactions between the system and an external actor that results in an outcome of value for the actor; name it verb + object ("Request a Chemical"). A user story: "As a [type of user], I want [goal] so that [reason]" — it also names the user class and the rationale. With use cases, the BA derives functional requirements and tests; a story is a placeholder for a just-in-time conversation, and epics are split to fit an iteration.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.

exercises.title: Usage-centric 3 — questions that find use cases
exercises.problemHtml:
Wiegers’ questions to discover use cases: What will the actor use the system for? Will they create, store, change, remove or read data? Will they inform the system of external events? Do they need to be informed of occurrences? For a smart-home system, which question surfaced each use case?

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.

exercises.title: Usage-centric 4 — turn a use case name into a user story
exercises.problemHtml:
For each use case of a library system write the equivalent user story in STORIES (keys UC1–UC3): UC1 "Reserve a Book" (primary actor: member), UC2 "Renew a Loan" (member), UC3 "Record a Returned Book" (librarian). Each must follow "As a <role>, I want <goal> so that <benefit>", name the primary actor of the use case as the role, and keep the use case’s goal.

Requirements

  • The benefit must be a real reason, not a repetition of the goal.
exercises.problemHtmlVi:
Viết user story tương đương cho ba use case thư viện; vai là actor chính, giữ mục tiêu của use case.

Yêu cầu

  • Lợi ích phải là lý do thật, không lặp lại mục tiêu.

examplesJson.output: As a member, I want to reserve a book that is on loan so that I can borrow it as soon as it is returned.

hintsJson: Vai = actor chính của use case.
Lợi ích trả lời "để làm gì".
